The vision of Engineering at the University of Guelph is to be one of the top-ranked engineering institutions in Canada by delivering a superior, design-based engineering education and relevant research programs that positively impact society and Improve Life.

Students can be part of medical innovation. The growing field of Biomedical Engineering fuses engineering design and problem solving to improve human health.

Biomedical Engineers apply the principles and technologies associated with engineering to design innovative ways to improve human health and quality of life. In this hands-on program, students will study anatomy, physiology and pathology as well as courses in electronics, mechanics, and computer science.

Students will examine bio-systems from molecular to a full body scale to understand what happens when something goes wrong, as in the case of injury or disease. Biomedical Engineering can also be an entry point into medical school.
xdq:
Computer Engineering focuses on the design and organization of computer systems. Graduates in Computer Engineering are able to apply mathematical, scientific and engineering principles to design and integrate computer systems suitable for applications in a wide range of fields. The program provides students with a common base of knowledge essential to computer engineering and then allows them to select electives to attain a degree of specialization in one of four areas or to choose electives to broaden their knowledge base. Elective concentrations are available in areas of Electronic Design automation, Software Design, Artificial Intelligence and Robotics, and Microsystems. Students will study and apply algorithmic, electronic and digital design principles to the design, construction, implementation and maintenance of software and hardware components of modern computing systems. As a graduate of Computer Engineering, students may be involved in circuit design and development, hardware integration, and system level design integration.

Sample Careers:

  • Computer design engineer
  • Software engineer
  • Hardware engineer
  • Artificial Intelligence developer
  • Wireless solutions engineer

The vision of Engineering at the University of Guelph is to be one of the top-ranked engineering institutions in Canada by delivering a superior, design-based engineering education and relevant research programs that positively impact society and Improve Life.

Computer Engineering fuses computer science with electrical engineering to develop systems and solutions for the technological industry.

Computer Engineering focuses on the science and tools behind designing, constructing, implementing and maintaining software and hardware components of modern computing systems. By emphasizing algorithmic, electronic, and digital design principles, the Computer Engineering program prepares students to develop effective and innovative technological systems and solutions. As a graduate of the program, they may be involved in circuit design and development, hardware integration, and system level design integration.

Mechanical Engineering at Guelph is built around concepts of sustainability and sustainable design to equip graduates to tackle issues associated with emerging technologies. Graduates in mechanical engineering are able to apply mathematical, scientific and engineering principles to a wide variety of fields and find employment across the private and public sectors. The program provides students with a common base of knowledge essential to mechanical engineering, and then allows them to select electives to attain a degree of specialization in one of five areas, or to choose electives which broaden their general knowledge base. Elective concentrations are available in the areas of wind and solar energy, food and beverage engineering, mechatronics, manufacturing system design and biomechanics.

Sample Careers:

  • Aerospace project coordinator
  • Manufacturing engineer
  • Robotics and automation engineer
  • Mechanical design engineer

Students in the Bachelor of Science - Animal Biology program will acquire a broad overview of animal production systems and a detailed understanding of how these rely increasingly on our emerging knowledge in fields such as genetics, molecular biology, reproductive technology, nutrition, environmental physiology, behaviour and welfare. The program provides excellent preparation for students interested in pursuing a career in veterinary medicine.

Sample Careers:

  • Animal bioscience specialist (research and education)
  • Animal behaviourist/animal care
  • Veterinarian
  • Product quality controller
90vd: The Master of Animal Biosciences (MABS) program is a professional, course-based degree designed for recent graduates and working professionals who wish to develop specialized, hands-on skills in animal science. The program can be completed in three semesters (one year) of full-time study and allows students to tailor their coursework to align with their individual interests and career goals. Areas of specialization include Animal Breeding and Genetics, Animal Nutrition and Metabolism, Animal Behaviour and Welfare, Animal Physiology, and Digital Animal Analytics. Students benefit from extensive practical learning in high-quality research and laboratory facilities focused on genomics, nutrient analysis, physiology, welfare, meats, and microbiology, gaining valuable applied experience that prepares them for diverse roles in the animal biosciences sector.
91u9:
A first-of-its-kind program in Canada, the Master of Applied Molecular and Health Sciences (MAMHS) is a one-year, course-based graduate program that integrates advanced molecular biology with emerging disciplines such as AI-driven drug discovery, immunology, and stem cell research models.

The program emphasizes both technical proficiency and professional development, preparing graduates for impactful careers in biotechnology, biomanufacturing, therapeutic development, and precision medicine.

Students study under the guidance of leading experts in immunology, genetics, bioinformatics, microbiology, and molecular biology, while gaining practical experience in state-of-the-art facilities equipped for tissue culture, microscopy, genomics, nuclear magnetic resonance, and mass spectrometry.

Throughout the curriculum, students engage with authentic, industry-relevant scenarios, including regulatory case studies, computational and AI-driven exercises, ethical dilemma debates, biomanufacturing scale-up challenges, and applied experimental projects.

With a strong focus on leadership, ethics, and scientific communication, the MAMHS program develops future leaders poised to advance the fields of biomedicine and biological science.
91on:
Individuals seeking to make a difference in healthcare can apply to the Master of Applied Nutrition (MAN) program, which prepares graduates for careers in nutrition and dietetics through three semesters of coursework and hands-on field experience.

The Master of Applied Nutrition program combines advanced professional coursework with competency-based experiential learning. Built on a foundation of critical appraisal and reflection, the program develops lifelong learners with adaptable, practice-based research skills. Upon graduation, students are equipped to apply their theoretical and technical knowledge of dietetics in a variety of professional settings.
91v9:
The Master of Arts in Financial Economics (MAFE) program offers rigorous training in economic theory, finance, and econometrics, providing students with a deep understanding of the analytical frameworks and quantitative tools essential for decision-making in financial and economic contexts.

Graduates of the program are well-prepared to pursue careers in economic analysis, banking, finance, policy development, and consulting across both the public and private sectors.

In addition, the program establishes a strong foundation for those seeking to advance to doctoral studies in economics or finance, equipping graduates with the theoretical insight and research skills required for advanced academic and professional success.
92hs:
The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence field prepares students to critically analyze and respond to these challenges by pairing philosophical reasoning with technical literacy and empirical understanding. Students learn how to examine fundamental questions—about fairness, accountability, privacy, autonomy, and the nature of intelligence itself—that underlie the applications of modern technologies.

Graduates are trained to become leaders who can bridge the gap between technology and human values, helping ensure that AI-driven innovations are designed and deployed in ways that are socially responsible and ethically sound. Through interdisciplinary coursework and collaborative research, students explore the theoretical and practical implications of emerging technologies, developing the insight to guide ethical decision-making in academia, industry, and public policy.
920i: The MA (Major Research Project) field offers a one-year, course‑based route through the Philosophy master’s program. It provides students with advanced training in philosophical scholarship while developing analytical, writing, and research skills applicable in academic and professional settings. The program culminates in a substantial but focused research paper that demonstrates the student’s ability to engage critically and independently with a philosophical topic.

Demand is accelerating for new approaches for data storage, retrieval, analysis, and applications. A new generation of professionals is required to meet this demand, having bioinformatics skills and the capacity to create new approaches.

The Master of Bioinformatics program is a three-semester course-based master’s degree, which provides life science graduates with the skills needed to work with the complex data now routinely generated by researchers across all disciplines. The program trains students in statistics, programming, and data analysis approaches so as to manage, analyze, and interpret large volumes of data from across science disciplines.

Thisprogram equips life science graduates with the skills needed to analyze datasets and develop new bioinformatics approaches. Students apply the skills learned through their courses to analyze data and create innovative bioinformatic methods, guided by two faculty members with extensive experience in the field.
91gn: The Master of Biomedical Sciences (MBS) program prepares graduates for careers in health care, veterinary medicine, government, and biomedical, pharmaceutical, or diagnostic research. It also provides a solid foundation for students planning to pursue thesis-based graduate studies, medical or veterinary school, or other competitive professional programs. This one-year, coursework-based program offers intensive graduate-level training without the requirement of a full thesis. The MBS program enables students to tailor their experience by choosing a field of study that aligns with their academic interests and career aspirations.
91gq: Master of Business Administration strengthens students’ business expertise while inspiring them to lead with responsibility and integrity. Through mastering core business areas such as operations, communication, and finance, students gain a strong foundation of knowledge and practical skills essential for success in today’s dynamic global environment. Guided by the Lang School’s mission of Business as a Force for Good®, the program places a strong emphasis on sustainability and responsible management, preparing graduates to make a positive impact in business and society.
